How to Convert a PDF to Word

Three ways to convert, change or transfer a PDF into an editable Word document: online with our converter, in Microsoft Word, or with Google Docs. Plus phones, Mac, scanned PDFs and quick fixes.

Quick answer: can you convert a PDF to Word?

Yes. A PDF is made for reading, not editing, but you can turn it into a Word document (.docx) and edit it like any other file. The quickest way is an online converter: upload the PDF, convert it, download the .docx. You can also open the PDF directly in Microsoft Word, or open it with Google Docs and download it as Word. Each method is explained below, with when it works well and when it doesn't.

How to convert PDF to Word with PDF2Wordly, step by step

  1. Open the converter and sign in. Go to the PDF to Word converter and log in with Google or email. A free account is enough.
  2. Upload your PDF. Drag the file into the drop area, or click "Choose PDF file". The file must be a PDF of 25 MB or less.
  3. Convert it. Click "Convert to Word". Pages with real text keep their text, images, tables and most of the formatting; scanned pages are read with OCR.
  4. Download and check. Click "Download Word" to save the .docx file, then open it in Microsoft Word, Google Docs, LibreOffice or Pages. Check tables and page breaks before you send it.

It runs in your browser, so there is nothing to install, on a computer, a tablet or a phone.

Free and Pro limits

  • Sign-in is required for every conversion, on Free and Pro.
  • Free account: 1 conversion every 24 hours, PDFs of up to 20 pages (20 scanned pages) and 25 MB.
  • Pro ($4.99/month): up to 100 files per day and up to 200 pages per file (scanned PDFs: up to 50). See the plans.
  • Your files: the PDF is deleted after conversion, and the Word file once you have saved it, within 1 hour at most.

How to convert a PDF to Word in Microsoft Word

Word for Windows (Word 2013 and later, including Microsoft 365) can open a PDF and turn it into an editable document:

  1. Open Word and choose File, Open, then pick your PDF (or right-click the PDF, choose Open with, then Word).
  2. Word warns that it will convert the PDF into an editable document and that it may not look exactly like the original. Click OK.
  3. Edit the text, then choose File, Save As and keep the type Word Document (*.docx).

Good for: simple, text-heavy PDFs when you already have Word. Watch out: page layouts, columns and tables often move; scanned PDFs don't come out as editable text; and you need a Word licence.

How to change a PDF to Word with Google Docs

  1. Upload the PDF to Google Drive.
  2. Right-click it and choose Open with, Google Docs. Google creates a new, editable Doc from the PDF.
  3. In the Doc, choose File, Download, Microsoft Word (.docx).

Good for: getting the text out of a short PDF for free, from any computer. Watch out: most of the layout, many images and table formatting are lost. Google's own help says its text recognition works on files up to 2 MB and reads only the first 10 pages.

How to convert a PDF to Word on a phone (Android or iPhone)

  1. Open pdf2wordly.com in Chrome, Safari or another browser, and sign in.
  2. Tap "Choose PDF file" and pick the PDF from Files, Downloads, Google Drive or iCloud Drive.
  3. Tap "Convert to Word", then "Download Word".
  4. Open the .docx with the Microsoft Word, Google Docs or Pages app to edit it.

More details for each device: PDF to Word on Mac, iPhone and Android.

How to convert a PDF to Word on a Mac

Use the converter in Safari, Chrome or Firefox: sign in, upload the PDF, convert, and the .docx goes to your Downloads folder. Open it with Microsoft Word, Pages or Google Docs. Copying text out of Preview also works for a few lines, but you lose the formatting.

What to do with a scanned PDF

A scanned PDF holds pictures of pages, not real text, so Word and simple converters give you images or nothing to edit. Our converter checks every page and reads the scanned ones with OCR, in English, French or Arabic. See scanned PDF to Word with OCR for how it works, tips for a cleaner scan and the page limits.

Common problems and how to fix them

  • The layout moved. Columns, text boxes and page breaks can shift in Word. Turn on Word's formatting marks to see what moved, and fix page breaks first. Converting the original PDF, not a printed-and-scanned copy, keeps more of the layout. More tips: PDF to Word without losing formatting.
  • A table came out in pieces or as text. Long tables can be split into several Word tables, and tables without grid lines can become plain text. Merge or rebuild them in Word; see PDF tables to Word.
  • The PDF has a password. A protected PDF can't be read. Remove the password you know first, then convert: password-protected PDF to Word.
  • The file is too large or has too many pages. Files are limited to 25 MB, and to 20 pages on a free account. Split the PDF or compress its images, then convert each part.
  • Fonts look different. If a font from the PDF isn't installed on your computer, Word shows a similar one. Install the font or pick another one in Word.
  • Something else failed. See PDF to Word not working.

Frequently asked questions

Can you convert a PDF to Word?

Yes. An online converter, Microsoft Word for Windows and Google Docs can all turn a PDF into an editable Word document. An online converter keeps the most layout and also reads scanned pages with OCR.

Is it free?

Yes, with a free account: 1 conversion every 24 hours, for PDFs of up to 20 pages and 25 MB. The Pro plan allows up to 100 files per day and up to 200 pages per file (scanned PDFs: up to 50).

Do I need an account?

Yes. You sign in with Google or email before converting. The account keeps the free daily conversion and the Pro limits fair for everyone.

How do I convert a PDF to Word without Microsoft Word?

Use the online converter in your browser, then open the .docx with Google Docs, LibreOffice or Pages. You don't need Word to convert, only to edit in Word itself.

How do I transfer a PDF into an existing Word document?

Convert the PDF to a .docx first, open it, copy the parts you need and paste them into your document. Use Keep Source Formatting when you paste to keep the look of the original.

Will the formatting stay the same?

Text, images and most tables and formatting carry over. Complex layouts with columns, text boxes or long tables may need small touch-ups in Word after the conversion.

Can I convert a PDF to Word on my phone?

Yes. Open the site in your phone's browser, sign in, choose the PDF from your files and download the Word file. It works on Android and iPhone.

Can I convert a scanned PDF to Word?

Yes. Scanned pages are read with OCR in English, French or Arabic. Scanned PDFs can have up to 50 pages per file with Pro and 20 with a free account.

Are my files kept private?

Files are sent over an encrypted connection and are never made public. The PDF is deleted after conversion, and the Word file is deleted once you have saved it, within 1 hour at most.
